content:
# Solution: Add Second Region to Crossplane Composition

To add us-west-2 support idiomatically in Crossplane without breaking existing claims, you need to:

1. **Add a second ProviderConfig** for the new region
2. **Extend the Composition** to parameterize region selection
3. **Update XRD (CompositeResourceDefinition)** with an optional `region` parameter
4. **Keep the claim schema backward-compatible** by defaulting to existing behavior

## Implementation

### Step 1: Create ProviderConfig for us-west-2

```yaml
apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-west-2
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-creds
      key: creds
  region: us-west-2
```

Keep your existing us-east-1 ProviderConfig:

```yaml
apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-east-1  # (or rename from "default" if necessary)
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-creds
      key: creds
  region: us-east-1
```

### Step 2: Extend the XRD with an Optional Region Parameter

Update your CompositeResourceDefinition to accept an optional `region` field:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: CompositeResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: xwebapps.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: XWebApp
    plural: xwebapps
  claimNames:
    kind: WebApp
    plural: webapps
  versions:
    - name: v1alpha1
      served: true
      referenceable: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                region:
                  type: string
                  enum:
                    - us-east-1
                    - us-west-2
                  default: us-east-1
                  description: "AWS region for deployment"
                environment:
                  type: string
                  enum: [dev, prod]
                # ... other parameters (clusterSize, nodeType, etc.)
              required:
                - environment
```

### Step 3: Update Composition to Use Region Parameter

Modify your Composition to dynamically reference the correct ProviderConfig:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: webapp-composition
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: XWebApp
  mode: Resources
  resources:
    # EKS Cluster
    - name: eks-cluster
      base:
        apiVersion: eks.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Cluster
        spec:
          forProvider:
            region: us-east-1  # Will be patched
            roleArnRef:
              name: eks-service-role
            resourcesVpcConfig:
              subnetIdRefs:
                - name: subnet-1
                - name: subnet-2
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-us-east-1  # Will be patched
      patches:
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.region
          toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.region
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.region
          toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
          transforms:
            - type: string
              string:
                fmt: "aws-%s"
    
    # S3 Bucket
    - name: s3-bucket
      base:
        apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Bucket
        spec:
          forProvider:
            acl: private
            versioningConfiguration:
              status: Enabled
            serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
              rules:
                - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
                    sseAlgorithm: AES256
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-us-east-1
      patches:
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.region
          toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
          transforms:
            - type: string
              string:
                fmt: "aws-%s"
    
    # RDS Instance
    - name: rds-instance
      base:
        apiVersion: database.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: RDSInstance
        spec:
          forProvider:
            dbInstanceClass: db.t3.micro  # Will vary by environment
            engine: postgres
            masterUsername: admin
            allocatedStorage: "20"
            backupRetentionPeriod: 7
            deletionProtection: false  # Will vary by environment
            multiAZ: false  # Will vary by environment
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-us-east-1
      patches:
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.region
          toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.availabilityZone
          transforms:
            - type: string
              string:
                fmt: "%sa"  # us-east-1a, us-west-2a
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.region
          toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
          transforms:
            - type: string
              string:
                fmt: "aws-%s"
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.environment
          toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.dbInstanceClass
          transforms:
            - type: map
              map:
                dev: db.t3.micro
                prod: db.t3.medium
        - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
          fromFieldPath: spec.environment
          toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.deletionProtection
          transforms:
            - type: map
              map:
                dev: "false"
                prod: "true"
    
    # ... other resources (IAM, ALB, etc.)
```

### Step 4: Deploy Without Changing Claims

Existing claims automatically work with the default region:

```yaml
# dev-claim.yaml - continues to work unchanged
apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
kind: WebApp
metadata:
  name: dev-web-app
spec:
  environment: dev
  # region defaults to us-east-1 if omitted
```

New claims can opt into us-west-2:

```yaml
# west-claim.yaml - new, explicit region
apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
kind: WebApp
metadata:
  name: prod-web-app-west
spec:
  environment: prod
  region: us-west-2
```

### Step 5: S3 Cross-Region Replication (Prod Only)

For prod environments with multi-region S3, add replication configuration to the composition:

```yaml
- name: s3-replication
  base:
    apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
    kind: ReplicationConfiguration
    spec:
      forProvider:
        bucketName: <interpolated from S3 bucket>
        role: arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/s3-replication-role
        rules:
          - destination:
              bucket: arn:aws:s3:::app-bucket-west-2  # Replica in us-west-2
              replicationTime:
                status: Enabled
                time:
                  minutes: 15
            filter:
              prefix: ""
            status: Enabled
  patches:
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.environment
      toFieldPath: metadata.annotations['crossplane.io/enabled']
      transforms:
        - type: map
          map:
            dev: "false"
            prod: "true"
```

## Key Design Points

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|---|
| **Backward compat** | `region` parameter defaults to `us-east-1`; existing claims unaffected |
| **No claim change** | Claim schema is extended only with optional fields |
| **Idiom** | Provider configs per region; composition patches select the appropriate config |
| **Environment separation** | Environment-specific behavior (replication, multi-AZ) via composition patches on `spec.environment` |
| **Multi-region resources** | S3 bucket deployed to primary region only; replication handled separately for prod |

This approach lets you deploy to us-west-2 by setting `region: us-west-2` in new claims while keeping all existing claims unchanged.
